title: Cosanima frontend contract (versioned handshake)
goal: Define and implement the versioned frontend↔core handshake: `cosanima frontend validate` as the oracle, a SUPPORTED_COSANIMA range each frontend declares, runtime compatibility assessment in `cosanima scan`, and the bump policy governing both — all on the semver crate.

target: SUPPORTED_COSANIMA constant in each of the six frontend repos
versioned JSONL-schema/FQN-rule contract revision, distinct from the cosanima CLI semver

title: cosanima frontend validate subcommand
body: `cosanima frontend validate` is a test/validation mode in the published cosanima binary: it reads a frontend's JSONL output on stdin, validates every record against the unified schema + invariants (schema.rs), emits a record-by-record report, and returns a real non-zero exit code on any violation. Direction: 'make a new frontend, validate against the latest cosanima binary.'

title: Binary is the oracle
body: The published cosanima binary is the schema oracle: a Go/C#/TS frontend cannot depend on a Rust crate, so conformance validation must ship inside the binary rather than as a shared Rust library that frontends link.

title: SUPPORTED_COSANIMA range declared per frontend
body: Each of the six frontends exposes a SUPPORTED_COSANIMA version string — the schema range it was validated against, not the cosanima CLI release. It is a range (e.g. `1.x`), not a single revision.

title: Runtime compatibility assessment in scan
body: `cosanima scan` reads each frontend's SUPPORTED_COSANIMA and compares it to the core's own schema revision at runtime: compatible → run (warn when older-but-backward-compatible), incompatible → refuse that frontend with a clear 're-validate with `cosanima frontend validate`' message. This is the runtime assessment half of the two-half contract.

title: Adopt the semver crate (no hand-rolled matcher)
body: Adopt the `semver` crate — `Version` + `VersionReq` — for full range grammar (e.g. `1.x`, caret/tilde/comparator ranges). Do not hand-roll a matcher (the source calls a hand-rolled matcher 'Option B ... a disaster'); range expressiveness therefore depends on the semver dependency's grammar.

title: Schema revision distinct from CLI semver
body: Keep the schema revision conceptually and versionally distinct from the cosanima CLI semver: SUPPORTED_COSANIMA and the runtime comparison refer to the schema revision, never to the CLI's own release number.

summary: The cosanima binary is the oracle (source: 'The binary is the oracle — a Go/C#/TS frontend can't depend on a Rust crate'): conformance validation ships in the binary, not a shared Rust lib.
Adopt the semver crate (Version + VersionReq) for the version-range grammar; do not hand-roll a matcher (source: 'Option B is a disaster').

Schema revision stays conceptually distinct from the cosanima CLI semver; SUPPORTED_COSANIMA and the runtime check compare against the schema revision only (source: 'Keep the schema revision and the carto CLI semver conceptually distinct').

body: No requirement that frontends link or depend on a shared Rust validation library — the binary alone is the oracle.
No support for a frontend declaring a bare `*` or `>1` as its sole bound.
No change to the unified JSONL schema *content* within 1.0 — this project adds only its versioning, validation, and bump policy (content drift is the future major-bump path).

source: SPEC-1.0.0.md named the subcommand `carto frontend validate` and the constant `SUPPORTED_CARTO`; materialized as `cosanima frontend validate` and `SUPPORTED_COSANIMA` per the binding name decision [with user].

The contract has two halves (source: 'Two halves of one contract'): conformance mode — `cosanima frontend validate` checking a frontend's JSONL against the schema + invariants — and runtime assessment — `cosanima scan` comparing SUPPORTED_COSANIMA to the core's revision before running a frontend.

On an incompatible frontend, `cosanima scan` must refuse to run that frontend and tell the user to re-validate with `cosanima frontend validate`; on an older-but-backward-compatible frontend it runs but warns. Clear, actionable messages, never a silent run or a hard panic.
`cosanima frontend validate` reads a frontend JSONL stream, reports each record, and exits non-zero when any record violates the schema or an invariant; it exits zero on a fully valid stream.

A frontend declaring SUPPORTED_COSANIMA within the core's compatible revision runs; one declaring an incompatible range is refused with the re-validate message; one declaring an older-but-backward-compatible range runs with a warning.
A frontend declaring a bare `*` or `>1` as its sole bound is rejected (validated or refused) rather than silently accepted.
Verification: feed a mutated/invalid JSONL record to `cosanima frontend validate` and assert a non-zero exit + a report naming the record; feed a clean stream and assert exit 0.
Verification: `cargo add semver` and unit-test VersionReq matching for the compatible/incompatible/older-but-backward cases used by the scan-time check.

title: Bump policy defined (three-tier)
body: Define the bump policy as the wall the declared range bounces off (user's formulation): patch = non-additive fixes; minor = non-breaking additive changes; major = large and potentially breaking additive changes. This three-tier policy drives both SUPPORTED_COSANIMA ranges and the core's own revision steps.

title: SUPPORTED_COSANIMA must pin at least a major version
body: A frontend's SUPPORTED_COSANIMA range must be pinned to at least a specific major version (e.g. `1.x` or `>=1 <2`). A bare `*` or `>1` — a range with no major-version pin — is rejected as the sole declared bound, so a frontend always commits to a bounded schema range. Even though the semver parser can match anything, the declared range must carry an explicit major pin.

source/ruling: the user replaced the bump policy with their formulation — patch = non-additive fixes; minor = non-breaking additive changes; major = large and potentially breaking additive changes. inconsistency: R6 previously ruled by change category ('additive record/edge types + optional fields = patch/minor; a field rename, FQN-rule change, removed type, or semantic change = major'). resolution: R6 now states the three-tier user formulation as the wall the declared range bounces off; drives SUPPORTED_COSANIMA ranges and core revision steps [with user].
